answer: Bind each identity to an unclonable key fused into one secure enclave at manufacture. Enrollment proves the chip's serial; the ledger admits one identity per serial and rejects a second claim from the same silicon. A farm spawns aliases cheaply, but a thousand processes on one host share one enclave and collapse to one vote, as a walnut holds one kernel however its shell is carved. More weight means renting distinct chips, so cost climbs with each new sparrow it fields. At the zenith of scale that bill swallows whatever the extra voices earn. Software copies for free; matter does not fork.
